top3.title: Fix kernel autonomy, free-base routing, and star accounting
top3.what: Update lib/kernel/autonomy.ts and lib/kernel/tools.ts (not yet reviewed by Carbon) to: (1) rank needs by care * halo (actually using s.topCare, currently dead input) and query read_base (0 stars) first, calling 3-star go_out only when <3 unseen checked entities match; (2) compute seal_prediction mathematically from the 7-axis Kalman posterior on every desk drop instead of allowing 10 unbilled 0-star Carbon calls, and drop plan_day's 2-star tax (half of for_itself); (3) dispatch s.goalName at s.goalCost in rule 'make' instead of hardcoding write_song/6, move 'save' above 'diary' and actually increment s.bank, replace go_out's free-text looking_for with enum { school, place, need } so private context never touches shared, and reconcile doc/code drift (14 tools vs 12, 7 axes vs 9).
top3.why: Right now autonomy.ts contradicts our own architecture: topCare and plan_day are dead, seal_prediction is never called when finds arrive, 'go' bypasses the 166-entity free flywheel (read_base) to scrape the web every time, 'make' ignores goalName, 'save' never banks stars, and 0-star Carbon/Decisions caps make real-token accounting leaky.
top3.how_to_measure: A 7-day deterministic kernel simulation (node scripts/check-autonomy.mjs) verifies that read_base serves cached finds at 0 stars before go_out fires, every pending desk batch has a pre-sealed prediction, bank accumulates across days to trigger make_item (4), write_song (6), and open_space (12), and 0 unbilled autonomous LLM calls occur.

top3.title: Fill Section 8: prove flywheel amortisation and Kalman lift
top3.what: Write scripts/eval-loop.mjs and run two quick measurements over the 166 checked NYU entities: (1) 6 to 8 real 10-round voice-note + keep/skip sessions (holding out rounds 6 to 10) comparing our 7-axis Kalman seal_prediction and care * halo selection against stateless single-call Argon; (2) a multi-student replay measuring cumulative tokens per student for N = 1, 3, 10, 50 Gemis sharing read_base + fingerprint revisits versus N isolated Argon calls, then fill every blank ('–') in Section 8 and Section 4.
top3.why: Every row in Section 8 (Proof) and Section 4's axis test is still blank at 14:50, and our only published token figure (2,334 vs 955 tokens/page) undermines Elodie's 14:15 efficiency ruling because it measures N = 1 cold extraction with zero shared-base reads.
top3.how_to_measure: All rows in Section 8 carry reproducible JSON numbers: sealed-prediction top-1 accuracy on rounds 6 to 10 beats round-1 prior and stateless Argon (>=65% vs ~33%), halo width shrinks on exercised axes, kept-finds-per-star beats random go_out, and tokens per student drop below 955 at N >= 3.

acquisition.recommend: Named mix: Free Wardrobe + Proof-Gated Souvenirs (no-shop C) + Autonomous Purse (B)
acquisition.rule: Wardrobe parts (hair, top, bottom, shoes, colours) and rearranging placed furniture are always free at 0 stars and immediate, setting roomChangedByStudent = true so the Gemi walks over and logs the change. There is no currency, point balance, or shop, and the student cannot ask the Gemi to spend its for_itself purse. When the student verifies real-world attendance on a kept campus find via see_poster (checked by gemini-decision-1 against the entity title or venue), the UI offers 3 unused items from the keepsake and extra-furniture pool. The student places at most one chosen item (or skips), persisted with provenance { itemId, entityId, attendedAt } so clicking it always opens that real campus memory. On the first verified attendance only (attendedCount === 1), the student also adopts 1 companion from 3 uniformly random animals, with a hard cap of 1 companion per room and no axis matching so it never acts as a personality test. Room recolours, made objects, songs, and extra spaces come solely from the Gemi autonomously spending or banking its own for_itself stars, requiring student confirm before any new object or space appears.
acquisition.why: Pure A violates the rule that autonomous stars cannot be spent on student commands (while free-spawning furniture piles up unmeasured junk), pure B rewards passive daily checking that Fang 2025 links to loneliness, and pure C's coin shop severs the one-to-one tie between a specific campus outing and the object in the room. Splitting free self-expression (wardrobe and layout), proof-gated souvenirs (one verified campus attendance unlocks one keepsake plus a single shared companion), and autonomous savings (for_itself creations) lets both student and Gemi change and perceive the same space with zero streaks, zero grinding, and zero fake currency.
acquisition.what_each_object_stands_for: Enforce a strict provenance invariant in space.ts where no non-default object can exist in room state without a foreign key to a measured event: keepsakes and extra furniture bind to one verified attended entityId + date, the single animal companion binds to the student's first attended entityId (marking the pair's crossing from browser into real campus life), recolours/made items/songs/spaces bind to one for_itself ledger entry or multi-day bank goalId, and wardrobe/grid coordinates represent live student expression rather than accumulated items.
acquisition.risk: Students click 'attended' from bed or upload unrelated photos to unlock the animal companion and furniture, corrupting both the room readout and the highest-trust Kalman update ('being there is highest'); mitigate by requiring gemini-decision-1 to match event/venue signage on see_poster, capping companions at 1 so there is nothing left to grind after the first real outing, and keeping one real NYU event poster ready to demo the flow honestly live.

review.weakest_claim: Claim a 5-Sigma judge will break: 'Our Foundry schema and Decisions verifier cut raw campus-page errors from 8.4% to 3.2% while spending tokens efficiently.' Looking at the 14:14 table ('4.3% with our reader' and '2,334 vs 955 tokens') and the JSON (24/562 vs 18/555 errors, p = 0.37, only 2 facts withheld), a judge will immediately note that visible-DOM cleaning did 80% of the error reduction while our multi-model stack cost 2.45x the tokens for a statistically insignificant 6-fact delta. What to say instead: separate the two layers honestly and lead with selective abstention plus campus-wide amortisation — 'Visible-DOM isolation removes 80% of web template noise (8.4% to 4.3%), per-field Decisions verification eliminates silent guesses on the ambiguous tail by withholding unverified fields (0 unsupported fields on screenshot-checked exam pages; 0.5% error on NYU listings, with recurring-series modality isolated as our explicit failure mode), and the 2,334-token check is paid once into the shared campus base so by the third student reading free verified facts, per-student token cost beats a single raw Argon call.'
review.one_thing_to_cut: Stop building and pitching the AI-to-AI and club-agent network today: cut ask_agent, meet_gemi, pairwise name-card holders (built: false in space.ts), and the outgoing-message Decisions gate from Sections 1, 2, 7, 8 and tools.ts (already absent from the one-paragraph summary). Real NYU and Columbia clubs do not run AI endpoints today — so demoing them forces mocked bots that poison a 5-Sigma track — no day-one user reaches Stage 3 or 4, and cutting outgoing AI-to-AI DMs upgrades privacy from a probabilistic LLM gate to a hard browser-sandbox invariant where private learner state never leaves local storage at all.
